turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): I must apologise, doctor. We are a little late. The parking was full and we had to go around twice.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please, that is quite alright. Do sit down. Was the traffic very bad?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Not too bad, thank you. Only the heat today is quite strong.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, his sister has been telling him to take biotin, the same tablets she takes for her hair. We did not buy any.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will leave the sister's biotin aside. What has brought you in today?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am having swelling in both my ankles, and I am passing urine very often.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swelling in both ankles, and passing urine often. When did the swelling begin, and does it change through the day?

[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm, I cannot say the exact day. It has been, err, about two or three weeks. It is milder in the morning, and worse by evening after I have been on my feet. If I put my feet up it settles a little.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The sock mark was there around that time, yes. He also keeps going to the bathroom.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the frequent urine, did that start with the swelling?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit earlier, doctor. Maybe one month. It is mostly through the day, not so much at night.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any burning or pain while passing urine?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. There is no burning and no pain.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath, or any swelling of the face?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): The water tablet I take in the morning, and after that the urine comes very frequently for some hours.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will come to the tablet. Just to be clear, any shortness of breath, or puffiness of the face?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I am not short of breath, and the face is not puffy.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Which medicines are you taking now?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I take amlo dipin five milligrams, one tablet every morning, for my blood pressure. And a water tablet, frusemide forty milligrams, one in the morning, by mouth.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is the amlodipine not ten milligrams? I thought the strip said ten.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No, please. It used to be ten milligrams, but it was reduced. For many months it is five milligrams only.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me summarise. Amlodipine five milligrams once every morning, and frusemide forty milligrams once every morning, both by mouth. You take them for high blood pressure.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, that is correct. The high blood pressure has been there for about eight years.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you miss any doses?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I take them daily. I am quite particular about it.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is very regular, doctor. I put the tablets out myself.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain or tightness when you walk?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): At home my machine this morning showed one thirty two over eighty four. It is often around that at home.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. We will look at the home numbers. Today in the clinic the blood pressure is 158 over 96, and the pulse is 76 per minute.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): That is higher than at home. I do become a little tense in the clinic, I am sorry.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): It happens. Let me examine you. There is pitting swelling of both ankles. The lungs are clear, and I hear no crackles.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything with the stomach or the bowels, acidity or loose motions?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. The stomach and bowels are quite normal.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): My working impression is that the ankle swelling is likely from the amlodipine, and the frequent urine is from the frusemide. I am not calling that a final diagnosis.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Will you change one of the tablets then?

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. We will stop the amlodipine, and I will start telmisartan forty milligrams, one tablet by mouth every morning, in its place, for the blood pressure. Please continue the frusemide forty milligrams every morning as before.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am arranging a kidney function blood test in the next day or two, before you start the telmisartan. Please come back in two weeks with the report, and kindly keep a note of the home readings.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. I will stop the amlodipine, and I will start the new tablet only after the blood test. Is there anything I should do for the swelling itself?

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please take less salt with your food, and rest with the feet up in the evening. If the swelling becomes suddenly much worse, or you become breathless, come sooner. Otherwise I will see you in two weeks.

spec.situation: Patient on amlodipine and a water tablet with swollen ankles and passing urine often; blood pressure read at clinic and at home with different numbers; doctor changes one medicine.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

omissions.text: Patient denied chest pain or tightness when walking was asked but not recorded.
Home blood pressure reading this morning was 132/84 mmHg, and patient says home readings are often around that.
Doctor stated lungs are clear on examination.
Patient reports taking both amlodipine 5 mg every morning and frusemide 40 mg every morning for high blood pressure.
Patient reports no missed doses and takes medicines daily/adherent.
Doctor instructed kidney function blood test should be done in the next day or two, before starting telmisartan.
Patient correctly repeated back the plan to stop amlodipine and start telmisartan only after the blood test.
